name: LSM6DS3TR-C
title: 6-axis IMU: 3-axis accelerometer and 3-axis gyroscope, I2C/SPI
summary: A 3-axis digital accelerometer (±2/±4/±8/±16 g) and 3-axis digital gyroscope (±125 to ±2000 dps) in one 2.5 × 3 × 0.83 mm 14-lead LGA, read over I2C or SPI. Both sensors draw 0.90 mA together in high-performance mode and run from 1.71 V to 3.6 V with a separate I/O supply down to 1.62 V. On chip are a 4 kbyte FIFO, a temperature sensor, a pedometer, tilt, wrist tilt, significant motion, tap, free-fall, wake-up and 6D detection, and an I2C master that reads up to four external sensors with hard/soft-iron correction for a magnetometer.

circuits.description: The module as a plain slave to one host over I2C or SPI (3- or 4-wire). VDD and VDDIO each get a 100 nF ceramic to ground right at the pin. The auxiliary pins SDx and SCx are unused and are tied together to ground or to VDDIO. SDA, SCL, CS and SDO/SA0 run to the host; for I2C, SCL and SDA each take a 10 kΩ pull-up to Vdd_IO. INT1 and INT2 are the two programmable interrupt outputs.

operation.text: Accelerometer and gyroscope power up and down on their own, each with its own ODR and power mode: accelerometer alone, gyroscope alone, or both. Writing a non-zero ODR_XL[3:0] in CTRL1_XL (10h) starts the accelerometer from power-down; ODR_G[3:0] in CTRL2_G (11h) does the same for the gyroscope.

Power-down, low-power, normal and high-performance. With G_HM_MODE = 0 in CTRL7_G (16h), every ODR from 12.5 Hz to 6.66 kHz runs in high-performance mode. With G_HM_MODE = 1, 12.5, 26 and 52 Hz run in low-power mode and 104 and 208 Hz in normal mode.

Power-down, low-power, normal and high-performance. With XL_HM_MODE = 0, every ODR from 12.5 Hz to 6.66 kHz is high-performance. With XL_HM_MODE = 1, 1.6, 12.5, 26 and 52 Hz are low-power and 104 and 208 Hz are normal. XL_HM_MODE is bit 4 of CTRL6_C (15h).

ADC, then an optional high-pass filter (HP_EN_G), then the optional LPF1 (LPF1_SEL_G, bandwidth by FTYPE[1:0]), then LPF2 at the output data rate, feeding the output registers and the FIFO. ODR runs from 12.5 Hz to 6.66 kHz.

An analog anti-aliasing filter, the ADC, a digital LPF1 and a composite filter. LPF1_BW_SEL in CTRL1_XL (10h) and INPUT_COMPOSITE in CTRL8_XL (17h) set the digital filtering. The composite filter offers a low-pass path (LPF2) and a slope or high-pass path; the output registers, FIFO, 6D, wake-up, activity/inactivity, tap and free-fall each take their data from points chosen by LPF2_XL_EN, HPCF_XL, HP_SLOPE_XL_EN, LOW_PASS_ON_6D and SLOPE_FDS. The pedometer, step functions, significant motion and tilt take the ODR/2 low-passed signal.

A 4 kbyte FIFO (up to 4096 16-bit words) can hold gyroscope, accelerometer, external sensor, step count with timestamp, and temperature data. Writes can be triggered by accelerometer/gyroscope data-ready (FIFO ODR no higher than either sensor's), sensor hub data-ready, or each detected step. Each data set can be decimated by 2, 3, 4, 8, 16 or 32 (FIFO_CTRL3, FIFO_CTRL4). FTH[10:0] in FIFO_CTRL1/2 sets a watermark; FIFO_STATUS1 to 4 report overrun, full, empty, watermark and the number of unread words, and INT1_CTRL/INT2_CTRL route these to the pins. Discard the first sample after switching into or out of FIFO mode.

Bypass (000) keeps the FIFO empty and is also how it is cleared. FIFO mode (001) fills until full and stops; STOP_ON_FTH = 1 caps the depth at the watermark. Continuous (110) keeps writing and drops the oldest data; an overrun sets OVER_RUN. Continuous-to-FIFO (011) runs continuous while the chosen trigger bit (in FUNC_SRC1, TAP_SRC, WAKE_UP_SRC or D6D_SRC) is 0 and switches to FIFO mode when it is 1. Bypass-to-continuous (100) stays reset while the trigger is 0 and runs continuous when it is 1.

Samples come out 16 bits at a time through the output pair at 3Eh (low byte) and 3Fh (high byte). The FIFO is arranged in four data sets of 6 bytes: 1st gyroscope, 2nd accelerometer, 3rd external sensor bytes SENSORHUB1 to 6, and 4th either SENSORHUB7 to 12, step count with timestamp, or temperature. A burst may begin by reading all four status registers.

I2C and SPI share pins. CS high selects I2C (and holds SPI idle); CS low selects SPI. SPI can be 4-wire or, with SIM = 1 in CTRL3_C (12h), 3-wire. Writing I2C_disable = 1 in CTRL4_C (13h) turns the I2C block off.

The part is an I2C slave in standard and fast (400 kHz) mode. SDA and SCL both need external pull-ups to Vdd_IO. The 7-bit address is 110101x: SDO/SA0 tied to supply gives 1101011b (6Bh), tied to ground gives 1101010b (6Ah), so two modules can share a bus. After the address and the 8-bit register sub-address, data follow MSb first; IF_INC in CTRL3_C sets whether the sub-address steps on each byte. A read uses a repeated START after the sub-address. A receiver not ready for the next byte may hold SCL low to make the transmitter wait.

The part is an SPI slave on CS, SPC, SDI and SDO. CS goes low for the whole transfer; SPC idles high while CS is high. Data change on the falling edge of SPC and are sampled on the rising edge. A transfer is 16 clocks: bit 0 is R/W (1 = read), bits 1 to 7 are the register address AD(6:0), bits 8 to 15 the data, MSb first. Each further 8 clocks moves another byte; IF_INC = 1 steps the address on each byte. In a read the part drives SDO from bit 8. In 3-wire mode the read data come back on SDA.

Mode 1: the part is an I2C or SPI slave to the host and SDx/SCx are tied to VDDIO or GND. Mode 2: in addition, SDx and SCx form an I2C master (MSDA, MSCL) that reads up to four external sensors, with INT2 able to serve as the master's external sync input MDRDY. The sensor hub master works in I2C fast mode only.

Up to six sensors in all: the two inside and four external on the master I2C bus. Bank A registers hold each external sensor's 7-bit address, a register sub-address, a read count and a read decimation; the bytes read land in SENSORHUB1_REG to SENSORHUB18_REG. The hub cycle is triggered by accelerometer/gyroscope data-ready or by an external signal on INT2 (START_CONFIG). Hard-iron offsets and a 3×3 soft-iron matrix can correct an external magnetometer (IRON_EN, SOFT_EN), and the raw magnetometer data appear at 66h to 6Bh. FUNC_EN and MASTER_ON must both be 1.

FUNC_CFG_EN = 1 in FUNC_CFG_ACCESS (01h) opens bank A (sensor hub, pedometer, significant motion, magnetometer correction); setting FUNC_CFG_EN_B as well opens bank B (absolute wrist tilt). Change embedded function registers only while the device is powered down.

A hardware tilt function, running on the accelerometer alone, raises an event at each change of the device tilt; its averaging window and threshold are programmable. With a phone in a front trouser pocket it fires on sitting down or standing up and stays quiet during walking, running or climbing stairs.

Raises an event when the angle between a chosen accelerometer semi-axis and the horizontal exceeds a threshold for at least a latency time. It works at 26 Hz on accelerometer data only and needs an accelerometer ODR of 26 Hz or higher. The default semi-axis is +X. Turn it on with FUNC_EN and WRIST_TILT_EN in CTRL10_C (19h); route it to INT2 with INT2_WRIST_TILT in DRDY_PULSE_CFG_G (0Bh), or read WRIST_TILT_IA in FUNC_SRC2 (54h), which also clears a latched interrupt. WRIST_TILT_IA (55h) names the axis. Threshold, latency and axis mask are in bank B.

Configurable interrupts for free-fall, wake-up, 6D/4D orientation, single and double tap, and activity/inactivity, plus low-power pedometer (step detector and counter), tilt and significant motion blocks. Basic interrupts are turned on by INTERRUPTS_ENABLE in TAP_CFG (58h) and routed with MD1_CFG/MD2_CFG. Inactivity can drop the accelerometer to 12.5 Hz low-power and put the gyroscope to sleep or power-down.

SDO/SA0, SDx, SCx, SCL and SDA come up as inputs without pull-up; INT1 and INT2 come up driven to ground; CS and NC pins 10 and 11 come up with internal pull-ups of 30 kΩ to 50 kΩ. The CS pull-up goes off with I2C_disable = 1. The SDO/SA0 pull-up comes on in 3-wire SPI; the SDx/SCx pull-ups come on with PULL_UP_EN.
The core runs from VDD. Fit 100 nF ceramic capacitors on VDD and VDDIO as near the supply pins as possible. Vdd is 1.71 V to 3.6 V; Vdd_IO is 1.62 V to Vdd + 0.1 V.

At rest on a level surface the X and Y accelerometer axes read 0 g and Z reads 1 g; the deviation from the ideal reading is the zero-g offset. Offset and zero-rate level come partly from stress on the MEMS element, so they can shift a little after soldering to a board or after heavy mechanical stress. The gyroscope output rises for counterclockwise rotation about an axis.

Data-ready is latched until the outputs are read, or a 75 µs pulse with DRDY_PULSED = 1. BDU = 1 holds an output register pair until both bytes are read; it is advised when reading the FIFO registers.
The LGA package is ECOPACK, RoHS and Green compliant and qualified for soldering heat per JEDEC J-STD-020.
